Engine component · reconciliation

Two sources disagree. One gets served.

Reconciliation is the stage that makes context correct. When two sources conflict on the same fact, Baltor doesn’t average them or pick the newest — it applies source precedence: the enforcing authority outranks the convenient copy. The winner is served with its citation; the loser is held out, never deleted. Pick a conflict:

The conflict

Same fact · two sources · one authority

Source precedence

Higher authority wins · highlighted = this conflict
stronger authority ↑  ·  weaker / more convenient ↓

What reconciliation guarantees

✓ One answer
No averaging, no “newest wins”
The enforcing authority is served — not a blend of conflicting sources or whichever was edited last.
✓ Loser held out
Surfaced, never deleted
The conflicting value is preserved with its handle as a warning — truth is never destroyed, only ranked.
✓ Decision recorded
Precedence rule + receipt
Why this source outranked that one is written into the receipt — the conflict resolution is auditable.
Reconciliation beside the rest. Picking the authority is one stage — the served fact is then hardened (anchored to a refreshable object), enhanced (citation attached), optimized and verified. Precedence is configurable per corpus, but the default always ranks the enforcing source over the convenient copy. See the guided demos for the full pipeline and the receipts explorer for the recorded decision. Not legal, medical, or financial advice — the source in force is the authority.
